methodological_rigor.justification: The study integrates WES, RNA-seq, and WGS across 137 TETs (20 SNUH + 117 TCGA) with murine scRNA-seq comparison, providing cross-cohort validation of three molecular subgroups. Appropriate statistical methods are applied throughout (Wilcoxon, Fisher exact, log-rank, Cox proportional hazards, Benjamini-Hochberg correction, permutation tests for amplification-timing confidence intervals), and the authors explicitly address technical challenges such as low tumor cell fraction by rescuing GTF2I mutations from RNA-seq and restricting analyses (tumor cell fraction >=0.4, diploid proportion >=0.8 for mutation-rate estimation). Experimental validation of IRS4 oncogenic function in HEK293T cells is included, with Western blot and IGF1R inhibitor response assays. Limitations include no formal power/sample-size calculation, use of only one non-TEC cell line (HEK293T) for mechanistic experiments, exclusion of metastatic tumors (acknowledged), and inconsistent multiplicity correction across exploratory immune/pathway comparisons.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a retrospective genomic/transcriptomic analysis of a surgical case series (SNUH) combined with the TCGA cohort, supplemented by in vitro mechanistic validation; best classified as Oxford LoE 4 (case series/low-quality retrospective cohort with preclinical mechanistic work). Clinical relevance is moderate: the three-subgroup classification could improve on the poorly reproducible WHO histologic system, and IRS4 is nominated as both an independent prognostic marker (Cox P=0.023) and a mechanism of resistance to IGF1R inhibition, suggesting a translational path. The CTLA4/CD80-CD86 colocalization and tertiary lymphoid structure findings also inform immune checkpoint strategy selection for this rare malignancy. However, no prospective validation, no direct clinical actionability demonstrated in patients, and endpoints are molecular/surrogate (RFS in retrospective analysis) rather than practice-changing.

reporting_quality.justification: REMARK is the most applicable standard given the biomarker/prognostic focus (IRS4, GTF2I, CN-type as prognostic classifiers), though elements of STROBE also apply to the cohort portion. The manuscript reports inclusion criteria, assay details, statistical methods, multivariate adjustment (gender, Masaoka stage, GTF2I/IRS4 status), and clinical covariates (Supplementary Table S1), and provides IRB/consent statements. Gaps include no explicit protocol pre-registration, no formal patient-flow diagram, no clearly reported handling of missing clinical data, and limited reporting of REMARK items on sample selection timeline and marker cutpoint derivation (the IRS4 >30 TPM cutpoint appears to be the median but is not pre-specified). Data-availability posture is weak as reported in the blinded text: TCGA data are publicly accessible by reference, but no deposition identifier is given for the 20 newly generated SNUH WES/RNA-seq/WGS samples or for the newly generated murine scRNA-seq, and no code repository is cited.

novelty_literature.justification: The study makes several specific advances beyond the prior Petrini 2014 and Radovich 2018 TCGA landscape papers: (i) rescuing GTF2I mutations from RNA-seq to reclassify 16 previously wild-type thymomas; (ii) explicit cross-species mapping of bulk TET transcriptomes onto a murine single-cell developmental atlas of TECs, assigning distinct cells of origin to each subgroup (TEP/cTEC for GTF2I-type, differentiated TECs for CN-type, tuft cells for thymic carcinoma); (iii) mutational-timing analysis showing early-life acquisition of chromosomal gains in CN-type thymomas; and (iv) nomination of IRS4 as a CN-type-specific oncogenic driver with experimental validation and prognostic significance. Novelty is tempered by prior work linking GTF2I knock-in to TEP impairment (He 2022, Giorgetti 2022) and the Yamada 2021 report of tuft-cell signatures in thymic squamous carcinoma, which the authors appropriately cite as corroborating rather than first-in-class. Overall a strong incremental-to-novel contribution in a rare tumor type.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with a logical arc from mutational landscape to transcriptional identity, pathway/metabolic biology, mutational timing, IRS4 mechanism, and immune profiling. The abstract is quantitatively grounded (cohort sizes, three-subgroup finding) and accurately previews the paper. Figure captions are detailed and standalone-interpretable, with specific statistical annotations (e.g., exact P-values, test identities). Terminology is defined on first use (TEC, TEP, cTEC, mTEC, TET), and the discussion appropriately contextualizes findings against Petrini/Radovich/He/Yamada prior work and acknowledges limitations (primary-only tumors, WGS depth, HEK293T non-TEC context implicit). Minor issues: results sections are dense and some pathway/immune analyses could be tightened; the abstract repeats a single-sentence summary verbatim.

key_strengths: Integrative multiomic design across 137 TETs with cross-cohort (SNUH + TCGA) and cross-species (murine + human scRNA-seq) validation of three molecular subgroups
Novel cell-of-origin mapping assigning TEP/cTEC, differentiated TEC, and thymic tuft cell origins to GTF2I-type, CN-type, and thymic carcinoma respectively
Mutational-timing analysis providing evidence that CN-type chromosomal gains initiate early in life, supported by both WGS and WES validation
Identification and experimental validation (HEK293T overexpression, PI3K/AKT activation, IGF1R-inhibitor resistance) of IRS4 as a CN-type-specific oncogenic driver with independent prognostic value
Technically rigorous handling of low tumor cell fraction, including RNA-seq rescue of GTF2I mutations and purity-restricted downstream analyses
key_concerns: No formal pre-specification/protocol registration and REMARK-style reporting of the IRS4 >30 TPM prognostic cutpoint is incomplete
Data-availability posture is weak as reported: no explicit deposition identifier for newly generated SNUH WES/RNA-seq/WGS or murine scRNA-seq, and no code repository cited
Mechanistic validation of IRS4 relies on a single non-TEC cell line (HEK293T) without a thymic epithelial model or in vivo confirmation
Study is limited to primary tumors; evolutionary trajectories to metastatic disease (and the TP53-driven axis) are acknowledged but not addressed
Clinical actionability remains hypothesis-generating (prognostic retrospective RFS, no prospective validation); no direct demonstration that subtype-informed treatment improves outcomes
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically solid, mechanistically coherent, and translationally meaningful integrative multiomics study of a rare tumor type; novelty and rigor align with mid-tier high-impact oncology venues (Tier 2) rather than practice-changing Tier 1, pending minor revisions on reporting and data/code availability.
